questions.question: Kala-azar disease is caused by ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Protozoa.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kala-azar **is a parasitic protozoan belonging to the class **Mastigophora or flagellata** caused by **Leishmania donovani**.
 
• **Leishmania donovani** is a human parasite that is dimorphic (i.e. shows two forms)& digenetic in nature.
 
• It causes the disease** Kala-azar or Dumdum fever by sand fly (phelobotomus).**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• This disease is spread by the bite of infected sand-fly, It can affect the** Skin (Cutaneous Leishmaniasis)**, the mucous membrane of the mouth, throat, and nose **(Mucocutaneous Leishmaniasis)**, Liver, lymph nodes, spleen, and bone marrow** (Visceral Leishmaniasis).**
 
• **Symptoms include** Cutaneous Leishmaniasis - Skin ulcers.
 
• **Mucocutaneous Leishmaniasis **- Ulcers in mouth, throat, and nose, Nosebleed, Difficulty in breathing.
 
• **Visceral Leishmaniasis** - Weakness, weight loss, loss of appetite, enlarged spleen, liver, lymph nodes, a decrease in the production of blood cells.

questions.question: Who among the following was one of the leaders of the Santhal rebellion?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Sidhu Manjihi.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Santhal Rebellion took place during** Lord Dalhousie (1848-1856) tenure at Rajmahal hills (in Jharkhand) led by Sidhu Manjhi.**
 
• Santhal uprising took place during 1855-56.
 
• **The tyrannical British revenue system, usury practices, and the zamindari system in India made Santhal peoples annoyed, and two Santhal brothers Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu organized 10,000 Santhals and proclaimed a rebellion against the British.**
 
• The Santhals are the largest tribal group in India found in **Jharkhand, WestBengal, and Odisha.**

 
• **Santhal Rebellion:**

 
 
• It was a rebellion against both the British colonial authority and zamindars by the Santhal people.
 
• **Leaders: Sidhu, Kahnu, Chand, and Bhairav.**
 
• **Location**: Jharkhand.
 
• The rebellion was suppressed and largely shadowed by other rebellions.
 
• To quell rebellion British created Santhal Pargana and special laws were

 passed protecting them.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Britishers invited the Santhals to come and settle in** Jharkhand promising land and economic amenities.**
 
• Thus Santhals from different states came to settle in today's Jharkhand.
 
• Later zamindars dominated these areas as they collected taxes and lent money at very high rates which the people could not generally pay and their lands were forcibly taken.
 
• This became the roots of the Santhal rebellion.
 
• In a fierce encounter, **Santhals were defeated **as they were fighting with bows and arrows while Britishers had modern weapons.
 
• Sidhu was caught in** August 1855 **and was hanged on a banyan tree at a place called** Panchkathia.**

questions.question: Nathu La Pass connects India with which of its neighbouring countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__China.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Nathu La is one of the highest motorable roads in the world. It is situated on the** Indo-Tibetan border 14450 ft.** above sea level.
 
• It is one of the most important Himalayan passes in the country. **Nathu means 'listening ears', and La means 'pass'**.
 
• It is one of the three open trading border posts between India and China and is famous for its picturesque beauty and beautiful environment.
 
• Nathu La is located on the** Old Silk Route**. It is a mountain pass in the Himalayas in the **East Sikkim district**.
 
• It** connects Sikkim to China's Tibet Autonomous Region**. It was sealed for almost 4 decades after the People's Republic of China suppressed a Tibetan uprising in 1959.
 
• The Nathu La Pass was **reopened in 2006** and since then, it has served as an **official Border Personnel Meeting(BPM)** Point.

questions.question: Collagen is a type of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Protein.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Collagens are available in large quantities the human body. They are found in skins, bones muscles, and tendons.
 
• Collagen is the main structural protein in the various connective tissues in the body. They are a primary structural component of connective tissues, such as skin and cartilage.
 
• Foods that are high in Collagen protein are- Chicken, fish, egg whites, citrus foods, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carbohydrate**

 
 
• It is a biomolecule consisting of Carbon, Hydrogen and Oxygen atoms. Carbohydrates are found in a wide array of foods-bread, beans, milk, popcorn, potatoes, cookies.
 
 
 
• **Fat**
 
 
• It usually means any ester of fatty acids. The following food are good sources of fat - avocados, tofu, nuts, seeds, fish, peanut butter, boiled and eggs.
 
 
 
• **Vitamin**
 
 
• Vitamin means 'vital for life'. It is an organic non-protein substance.
 
• Vitamins are compounds necessary for the healthy functioning of our bodies.
 
• We need vitamins to help us grow, to see correctly, as well as to help us battle infections.
 
• It is required by an organism for normal metabolic function but cannot be synthesized in sufficient quantity by that organism.
 
• They are also required in small quantities to prevent deficiency diseases.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first Indian to win a seat in the House of Commons?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Dadabhai Naoroji.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• First Indian elected to the British House of Commons, **Dadabhai Naoroji** contested on the ticket of **Liberal Party.**
 
• Dadabhai Naoroji was also known as the **"Grand Old Man of India" and "Unofficial Ambassador of India"**.
 
• He was an Indian political leader, merchant, scholar and writer who was a Liberal Party Member of Parliament in the **United Kingdom House of Commons between 1892 and 1895.**
 
• Naoroji is honoured for his work in the Indian National Congress, of which he was one of the founding members and thrice - **in 1886,1893, and 1906 - elected president.**
 
• His** authored book Poverty and Un-British Rule in India** brought attention to his theory of the Indian **"wealth drain"** into Britain.
 
• India Post showing Naoroji on stamps in** 1963, 1997 and 2017.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Liberal Party**:

 
 
• Liberal Party, a British political party that emerged in the** mid-19th century as the successor to the historic Whig Party.**
 
• It was the major party in opposition to the Conservatives until **1918, after which it was supplanted by the Labour Party**.
 
• The Liberals continued as a minor party until** 1988** when they **merged with the Social Democratic Party to form what is now called the Liberal Democratic Party.**
 
• Through its long history, the Liberal Party included various schools of thought, but all Liberals were united by the conviction that the source of progress lay in the free exercise of individual energy.
 
 
 
• **Labour Party**:
 
 
• Labour Party, **a British political party whose historic links with trade unions have led it to promote an active role for the state in the creation of economic prosperity and in the provision of social services.**
 
• In opposition to the Conservative Party, it has been the **major democratic socialist party in Britain since the early 20th century.**
 
• In 1900 the **Trade Union Congress (the national federation of British trade unions) cooperated with the Independent Labour Party(founded in 1893) to establish a Labour Representation Committee,** which took the name Labour Party in 1906.
 
 
 
• **Conservative Party**:
 
 
• **Conservative Party, byname Tories, in the United Kingdom,** a political party whose guiding principles include the promotion of private property and enterprise, the maintenance of a strong military, and the preservation of traditional cultural values and institutions.
 
• Since World War I the Conservative Party and its principal opponent, the Labour Party, have dominated British political life.
 
• The name Conservative was first used as a description of the party by **John Wilson Croker writing in the Quarterly Review in 1830.**
 
 
 
• **Communist Party:**
 
 
• ** The Communist Party of Britain (CPB) is a communist political party in Great Britain idealized to Marxist-Leninist theory.**
 
• The party came out from a dispute between Eurocommunists and Marxist-Leninists in the Communist Party of Great Britain in 1988.
 
• Ex-members included General Secretaries of three organisations:
 
• **Bob Crow of the RMT union, Ken Gill of the Manufacturing.**
 
• **Science and Finance (MSF) union and member of the TUC General Council.**
 
• **Kate Hudson of the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament (CND). **

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Asiatic Society at Calcutta (Kolkata) founded by Sir William Jones?

• It was visualized as a centre for Asian studies including everything concerning man and nature within the geographical limits of the continent.

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of human wants in terms of economics?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Wants are satiable.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Human wants are** unlimited**; There is no limit to man's wants so any particular want is **satiable.**
 
• **Want is often thought of as a psychological desire** which makes life just a little more enjoyable, but which is not physiological necessary to life.
 
• You need oxygen, but you want a hot fudge sundae.
 
• **Satisfaction is achieved by fulfilling wants.**
 
• Wants are the form taken by human needs when shaped by culture and individual personality.
 
• When backed by buying** power wants become demands companies address needs by putting forth a value proposition**, a set of benefits that they promise to consumers to satisfy their needs.

questions.question: A fuse protects an electric circuit from:

options.text: converting one form of energy into other

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Overloading.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An electric fuse is a safety device **used to limit the current in an electric circuit which melts and breaks the circuit whenever there is an excess flow of current** through the circuit.
 
• A fuse is usually a short piece of wire and is installed in a circuit to stop the flow of excessive current.
 
• The material of the fuse has** high resistivity and a low melting point.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Functions of Electric Fuse:**

 
 
• It acts as a barrier between an electric circuit and the human body.
 
• It prevents any damage to the electric device by restricting excess current flow.
 
• It prevents overloading of current.
 
• It prevents the damage caused by the mismatch of the load.
 
• It prevents blackouts.

questions.question: Which of the following states does the capital of India, Delhi share its border with?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is 'Haryana'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Haryana:**

 
 
• Delhi, the capital of India, shares its border with the state of Haryana.
 
• Haryana surrounds Delhi on three sides: in the west, north, and south.
 
• Major cities in Haryana such as Gurugram, Faridabad, and Sonipat are in close proximity to Delhi, making these areas part of the National Capital Region (NCR).
 
• The extensive connectivity between Delhi and these nearby regions in Haryana facilitates a significant socio-economic interaction.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Punjab:**

 
 
• Punjab does not share a border with Delhi.
 
• It is located to the northwest of Haryana and has distinct geopolitical boundaries separated from Delhi by the state of Haryana.
 
• Punjab is renowned for its rich agricultural land, history, and Punjabi culture, but it does not have direct geographical adjacency to Delhi.
 
 
 
• **Himachal Pradesh:**
 
 
• Himachal Pradesh is a northern state known for its mountainous terrain and does not share a border with Delhi.
 
• The state's boundaries are adjacent to Punjab, Haryana, and Jammu and Kashmir, but it lies further to the north compared to Delhi.
 
• Himachal Pradesh's geographical separation from Delhi is significant enough that it does not influence Delhi's immediate socioeconomic dynamics.
 
 
 
• **Jammu and Kashmir:**
 
 
• Jammu and Kashmir, comprising the northernmost part of India, does not share a boundary with Delhi.
 
• It is separated from Delhi by a considerable distance, with the states of Punjab and Himachal Pradesh lying in between.
 
• Jammu and Kashmir's proximity to the western Himalayan range marks its distinct geographical and cultural landscape, separate from Delhi's border dynamics.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Delhi also shares its border with the state of Uttar Pradesh apart from Haryana.
 
• Uttar Pradesh lies to the east of Delhi and includes important nearby cities such as Noida and Ghaziabad, which are also part of the NCR.
 
• The National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi is a significant area for India's administration, geography, and urban planning, influencing multiple surrounding states.

questions.question: Glucagon, a peptide hormone, is produced by the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Pancreas.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The pancreas is a compound **(both exocrine and endocrine)** elongated organ situated between the limbs of the** 'C' shaped duodenum,99% part of the pancreas is exocrine while only 1% part is endocrine.**
 
• **The exocrine portion (acini cells) **secretes an alkaline pancreatic juice containing enzymes and the endocrine portion (islets of Langerhans) secretes hormones - **insulin, glucagon & Somatostatin**.
 
• The islets of Langerhans has 3 types of cells **A cells, B cells, and the 8-cells**.
 
• **The cells surround the B cells.**
 
• **Insulin is secreted by the B cells.**
 
• **Glucagon is secreted by the A cells.**
 
• The hormone somatostatin is secreted by the** 6-cells (Delta Cells).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The hormones insulin & glucagon are very important for sugar metabolism.
 
• Insulin is released into the bloodstream to lower down blood sugar levels and prevent hyperglycemia.
 
• Glucagon is released into the bloodstream to prevent blood sugar levels from dropping too low (hypoglycemia).
 
• Somatostatin is a growth-inhibiting hormone, it inhibits the secretion of several other hormones.

questions.question: Which of the following Amendment Acts of the Constitution of India conferred statehood to Goa and formed a new union territory comprising of Daman and Diu?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__56th Amendment Act.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **56th Constitution Amendment **

 
 
• Under this amendment, on 30 May 1987, Goa was given the status of a separate state.
 
• Goa became the 25th state of India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Amendment**
 **Subject**
 
 

 **23rd Amendment Act**
 
 
 
• It is officially known as The Constitution (Twenty-third Amendment) Act, 1969, **discontinued reservation of seats for the Scheduled Tribes in Nagaland**, both in the Lok Sabha and the State Legislative Assembly.
 
 
 
 

 **67th Amendment Act**
 
 
 
• The Constitution (Sixty-seventh Amendment) Act, 1990 Amendment of Article 356.
 
• In Article 356 of the Constitution, in clause (4), in the third proviso for the words** "three years and six months", the words "four years"** shall be substituted.
 
 
 
 

 **45th Amendment Act**
 
 
 
• It is officially known as The Constitution (Forty-fifth Amendment) Act, 1980, **extended the period of reservation of seats for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and representation of the Anglo-Indians** in the Lok Sabha and the State Legislative Assemblies.
